title: Concordance query answer
description: Schema of the JSON answer of concordance query: the model it was read from, the entity the expression names, where the entity is used, what it is linked to, and the decisions and sessions among those links.

model.description: The model the answer was read from.

file.description: The model file as named on the command line.

at.description: ISO 8601 date of the build that wrote the model.

tool.description: Version of the command line that wrote the model.

sources.description: The sources of the model, `name@commit` when the build recorded a commit.

age.description: The age of the model worded from the clock of the command; absent with --no-age.

entity.description: The entity the expression names, exactly as `model.json` serialises it under `entities` (see the model schema).

occurrences.description: Where the entity is named, grouped by the note whose files hold the occurrences.

notes.description: The notes listed under the bound, by source then identifier.

source.description: Name of the source holding the files.

note.description: The note whose files hold the occurrences; absent when no note of the model owns the file.

occurrences.description: The occurrences listed under the bound, by path then line.

path.description: Forward-slash path of the file relative to its source.

method.description: The method of the link that recorded the occurrence; absent for a passage of a keyword page.

more.description: Occurrences of the note the bound left out.

links.description: The entities linked to the queried one, best confidence first.

entries.description: The links listed under the bound.

related.description: The decisions and the sessions linked to the entity, every one of them, best confidence first.

linked.description: One entity linked to the queried one.

domain.description: Domain of the linked entity, when it has one.

relation.description: Relation of the link, a slug of the profile.

direction.description: `out` when the queried entity is the source of the link, `in` when it is the target.

confidence.description: Combined confidence of the link, in [0, 1].

methods.description: The methods that claim the link, in code-unit order.
